Facilitator Guide.docx.p2: I teach twelve two-hour sessions through one fictional legal and tax matter, building on the learner’s existing use of Claude, ChatGPT and similar assistants. I operate the demonstrations while the learner checks evidence, explains mechanisms and directs decisions. We complete the working records in class. The read-aloud notes explain the concepts; the detailed demonstration instructions below supply the teaching sequence.
Facilitator Guide.docx.p6: I establish the transaction trigger before applying a consent exception. I keep missing facts unresolved, distinguish the agreed text from a proposed amendment and check related provisions before describing a remedy.
Facilitator Guide.docx.p8: Before teaching I open the session run sheet, the required practice files and the checked instructor references. I test the account route and keep the saved observed run available. I describe a feedback-assisted revision as a revision, rather than a first-pass success.
Facilitator Guide.docx.p10: Each session totals 120 minutes, including a five-minute break and a ten-minute transfer check. That final block also provides recovery time when setup runs late. I use the core sequence first; optional material sits outside the plan. No homework is required.
Facilitator Guide.docx.p12: The workbook holds prompts and working records. Teaching Resources holds Classroom Run Sheets.txt, Checked Contract Answers.txt and Checked Goal Relief Case Note.txt. I use Source Review Workflow.txt and Research Verification Workflow.txt to check outputs before accepting them.
